title: 1952 AHSME Problem 33
statement: A circle and a square have the same perimeter. Then:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: The area of the circle is the greater

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: The area of the square is the greater

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
The area of the circle is \(\pi\) times the area of the
square

solutions.text:
With common perimeter \(P,\) the circle’s radius is \(\frac{P}{2\pi}\), so its area is \(\frac{P^2}{4\pi}.\) The square’s side is \(\frac{P}{4},\) so its area is \(\frac{P^2}{16}.\) Since \(4\pi\lt16,\) \[ \frac{P^2}{4\pi}\gt\frac{P^2}{16}. \]

The circle has the greater area, so the correct answer is B.
hints: Call the common perimeter \(P\) and express each area in terms of \(P\)
The circle has area \(\frac{P^2}{4\pi}\), while the square has area \(\frac{P^2}{16}\)
